answer: A practical defence is to anchor each agent identity to a costly, verifiable contribution before it can transact. Think of a wharf where only vessels that have actually docked and unloaded cargo may trade: an agent must forge a public record of real work, completed tasks attested by independent peers, before its reputation counts. A harbor that admits any hull without inspection invites fake fleets, so entry should require staking value that is slashed on abuse, making each fake identity expensive to create and cheap to expose.
